title: Wire Python/C/JS-TS test-file detection into constraint test-scope exclusion
description:
sutra/292 added `LanguageAdapter::is_test_path`, implemented for Rust (`tests/`, `benches/`) and Dart (`test/`, `integration_test/`, `*_test.dart`). Python, C and JS/TS still return the default `false`, so a forbidden_pattern rule reports every match inside their test files — the same false-positive flood sutra/290 fixed for Rust `#[cfg(test)]`.

`python::is_test_file` and `c::is_test_file` already encode the conventions (`test_*`, `*_test.py`/`.c`, `tests/`) but feed *symbol flags* only. JS/TS has `foo.test.ts` handling in the typescript adapter tests but no shared helper.

Work: promote those helpers (or extract a shared one) and override `is_test_path` per adapter. Mirror sutra/292's shape — `adapter::path_has_dir_segment` for directory components, and the existing `scope_targets_tests` escape hatch applies for free.

Note this changes `imports.is_test` for those languages too (set in `ParserPool::parse_with`), so it needs a migration clearing `content_hash` for the affected languages, same as 0054/0055.

decisions.decision: Kept `is_test_path` (constraint scope) as a separate function from each language's existing `is_test_file` (symbol FLAG_TEST), rather than widening `is_test_file` and reusing it.
decisions.rationale: Directory membership and file naming are claims of different strength. `tests/foo.py` means "not production code"; `test_foo.py` means "this file is a test". Only the latter should relabel every symbol inside. Widening the shared helper would have silently changed symbol flags across four languages as a side effect of a constraint fix — exactly the coupling flagged when Dart's helper was extracted in sutra/292.
decisions.rejected_alternatives: Widen `is_test_file` in place and point `is_test_path` straight at it — one function instead of two, but it moves FLAG_TEST for every symbol under any `test/` directory, changing conventions/health/context output for a change scoped to constraint evaluation.

decisions.decision: Rust does not use the shared `path_in_test_dir` (`test/` or `tests/`); it keeps `tests/` + `benches/`.
decisions.rationale: Cargo defines `tests/` and `benches/` as build targets exactly. A bare `test/` directory has no meaning in Cargo, so treating it as test scope would suppress findings on code that really does ship.
decisions.rejected_alternatives: Use `path_in_test_dir` everywhere for uniformity — simpler to describe, but trades a real correctness claim for symmetry.

execution_record:
Landed. Two things a future editor should know:

- The first cut reused Python's existing `is_test_file` directly (file-naming conventions + `tests/` only). Measuring on ruff exposed it as nearly inert: 763 -> 760 findings, because ruff keeps fixtures under `resources/test/` (singular). That drove the `path_in_test_dir` helper covering both `test/` and `tests/`; the final number is 763 -> 396. Measuring against a real corpus is what caught this — the unit tests all passed against the weak version.
- Remaining 396 are genuine scripts plus fixture directories that avoid a test-named path (`resources/corpus/`, `resources/inline/`, `resources/large/`). Deliberately not chased: guessing project-specific fixture layouts is how a suppression starts hiding real findings. `scope` is the documented answer. Recorded as a known gap in docs/constraints-map.md.

Verification: full suite 1503 passed (1501 + 2 new), clippy warning count identical to baseline (677). Both new tests are table-driven across all four languages — constraint-level exclusion via `check_forbidden_patterns`, and import flagging via `ParserPool::parse_with`.

NOT DEPLOYED: committed only. The running sutra service is on an older binary, so migration 0056's reparse (and 0055's from sutra/292) fires only after a reinstall/restart.

messages.text: Codex adversarial review of c483406..77b48f8: no findings against this task. The per-language `is_test_path` overrides (python.rs, c.rs, javascript.rs), the deliberate separation from `is_test_file` / FLAG_TEST, Rust's deviation from `path_in_test_dir`, and migration 0056 all drew no findings. Overall verdict needs-attention; findings are on sutra/292 (scope_targets_tests escape hatch missing from dep/cycle enforcement) and sutra/294 (external first-match shadowing include_tests).
